title: ASAS-3 eclipse times from 2001-2009 confirm the 1.6-year third body of HD 303514 and, with TESS times, limit its mass to 1.8-4.1 solar masses for a 4-solar-mass binary
abstract: HD 303514 is a detached 19.897-day eclipsing binary whose eclipses became shallower from 2002 to 2026. SCI 90287c11 explained a TESS (2019-2026) timing variation with a third body on a 1.6-year, near-coplanar orbit, but found no upper limit on its mass. We used the raw ASAS-3 V photometry (2000-2009; 808 points, 98 inside eclipses) as an independent timing data set. ASAS-3 alone shows a timing variation: a sinusoidal term decreases chi-square by 32 at 550-600 d (semi-amplitude 46 min), or at its one-year alias near 1,050 d. Two other apertures give 33 and 20. We integrated 17 published three-body solutions back to 2001. They did not use these times. The TESS-only near-coplanar solution predicts them: with a free linear ephemeris it is better than a linear ephemeris alone by 14.0 in chi-square. Near-polar solutions are worse by 626-1,358, and published fits with third-body masses of 4.5-12 solar masses are worse by 73-417. A joint photodynamical fit of the TESS times and geometry and all ASAS-3 points (REBOUND three-body model, twin-star eclipses) gives m3 = 3.2 solar masses for an inner pair of 4 solar masses, outer period 597.3 d, e2 = 0.21 and mutual inclination 2.9 deg (chi-square 798.5 for 835 data). A profile over fixed m3, with continuation from both sides, gives m3 = 1.8-4.1 solar masses at delta chi-square 4 and 1.3-4.7 at 9; m3 = 6.5 is worse by 30. Limits on the light fraction of the binary do not change this. No accepted solution loses its primary eclipses before 2045. The shallowest eclipses occur in 2028-2036 at 8-76 percent of the 2026 depth, depending on the poorly constrained light fraction. For m3 <= 1.7, the secondary eclipses can stop for a short time. Limitations: a twin-star model with a fixed inner mass, a multimodal likelihood with local fits and no MCMC, Gaussian noise, and an extrapolated forecast. A main-sequence third star of this mass would be too bright for most fits, so the third body is probably underluminous.

Left: ASAS-3 chi-square of published profile solutions relative to a linear ephemeris. Right: chi-square profile of the joint TESS + ASAS-3 fit over the third-body mass m3 (M12 = 4 solar masses).

citations.reason: Uses its TESS eclipse times, geometry, three-body code and solutions. Independent ASAS-3 times confirm its near-coplanar third body and reject the near-polar family; the joint fit adds an upper mass limit and changes the forecast depth minimum.
ASAS-3 selection rules, reference ephemeris and discovery of the HD 303514 eclipse fading.
Its eclipse-loss forecast near 2030 is not supported by the dynamical model fitted to TESS and ASAS-3 times.
Earlier campaign work on orbital-plane changes in TESS eclipsing binaries.
Analogous photodynamical solution of the vanishing-eclipse system HD 93683.
